rgb: The setting is an outdoor stone-paved yard, with rows of grey moulded egg trays spread across the ground on the left and centre, a wheeled multi-level metal rack holding blue boards and trays on the right, and a green building approximately 25 to 35 metres away in the background. At the bottom foreground, within arm's reach and about 0.3 to 0.6 metres below and ahead of the viewpoint, the camera wearer carries a flat blue board loaded with egg trays, partly cut off by the lower edge of the frame. In the first frame, the wheeled rack sits 1 to 2 metres to the right and is partially outside the right edge; a red-shirted person stands 4 to 5 metres ahead, facing and looking at the camera wearer while within arm's reach of the rack, and a black-shirted person is 5 to 6 metres ahead, roughly 1.5 to 2 metres left of the person in red, bent over the ground trays while facing left and holding a blue board. Through the second and third frames, the viewpoint rotates left and angles downward at the ground trays 1 to 6 metres away, sending the rack and the person in red out of sight to the right; only the black-shirted person's legs and board remain briefly visible along the upper-right edge of frame two. In the fourth frame, the viewpoint points directly downward, revealing the camera wearer's hands grasping the tray-loaded blue board about 0.4 metres away above their feet, with the board partly blocking the pavement underneath. The viewpoint then lifts and turns right in the fifth frame, where the held blue board is now empty at bottom-centre and the person in black stands upright 4 to 5 metres ahead, facing the wearer with a blue board in hand, slightly ahead of and about 1 metre left of the person in red, who likewise faces the wearer beside the rack.
depth: The depth map depicts an open paved outdoor courtyard, with rows of egg cartons across the left side and a wheeled, multi-tier rack of blue boards on the right. In every one of the five frames, the camera wearer holds a blue board below the viewpoint and within arm's reach, approximately 0.3–0.6 m away. Frame 1 shows two workers ahead and left of the rack: the worker in red stands upright about 4–5 m away facing the wearer, while the worker in black bends over around 1.5 m to his left at a distance of about 5–6 m. Across Frames 2–4, the wearer turns left and angles the view down toward the ground roughly 1–2 m away, then rotates right in Frame 5 to face the rack about 1–2 m away on the right and both workers about 4–5 m ahead. The workers are around 1 m apart, both face the wearer, and the worker in black holds a board within his reach. In Frame 4, the bright foreground distinctly separates the raised blue board and cartons at about 0.4–0.5 m, together with the wearer's supporting right arm and partly hidden left hand, from the darker ground and left foot approximately 1.2 m directly beneath. Relative to RGB alone, the uninterrupted luminance gradient makes both the receding ground plane and the vertical height difference between the carried board and floor immediately clear, even where the repeated carton patterns weaken perspective. Still, the map is unreliable around the rack's thin metal frame, which blends into the background depth, and in Frame 4, where the ground looks unusually dark compared with Frames 2 and 3 despite being viewed from a similar distance.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation map separates individual foreground and background entities throughout the courtyard. In Frame 1, it detects three people: the black-clad worker bending at centre-left about 5–6 m away, the upright worker in red at centre about 4–5 m away and approximately 1.5 m to the first worker's right, and a very small distant figure roughly 15–20 m away behind the first worker's shoulder. The ground, egg cartons, and wheeled rack receive no segmentation. When the camera wearer turns left and looks downward in Frame 2, only a person's lower legs remain visible at the upper-right edge, around 3–4 m away. Frame 3 contains no masks whatsoever as the viewpoint looks at the ground arrangement of cartons about 1–3 m away. At close range in Frame 4, approximately 0.3–1.2 m, the map identifies the wearer's outstretched right arm at lower right and left foot at lower centre as separate person instances within arm's reach. Frame 5 again detects the two upright workers standing side by side about 4–5 m ahead and roughly 1 m apart, with the worker in black slightly closer and partly blocking the rack next to the worker in red. Compared with RGB alone, this map makes the tiny faraway person in Frame 1 easier to notice and more clearly separates the workers' overlapping outlines in Frame 5. Its object classes and completeness are nevertheless highly unreliable: it labels two moulded egg cartons on the carried board in Frame 4 as 'pizza' and a blue rack shelf in Frame 5 as 'boat', while omitting the wearer's partly occluded left hand in Frame 4 and every other board and carton.
pose: Against a black background, the pose map displays 2D skeletal keypoints and detects only three subjects across the sequence: the standing worker in red in Frame 1 about 4–5 m ahead and left of the rack, the camera wearer's own right hand in Frame 4 about 0.4 m ahead at lower right, and the worker in black in Frame 5 roughly 4 m ahead at centre-right. In Frame 1, a yellow body skeleton portrays the red-shirted worker standing in three-quarter profile, facing forward and slightly left, with his head directed toward the camera wearer and his arms hanging within reach of the neighbouring rack. The bent worker approximately 1.5 m to his left is missed entirely. Frames 2 and 3 have no skeletal detections: the nearby person at Frame 2's top-right is largely outside the image above the knees, while Frame 3 contains only the ground and the held board's bottom edge. In Frame 4, a magenta hand skeleton marks the bent fingers and thumb of the wearer's right hand as it grips the blue board's lower edge within arm's reach. In Frame 5, a yellow body skeleton depicts the worker in black facing the camera wearer, with both elbows flexed and both forearms lifted to support a board at chest level. The skeletons reveal the precise finger articulation beneath the board edge in Frame 4 and the limb-joint locations in Frames 1 and 5 more clearly than RGB alone. Even so, the map is unreliable because it omits the bent worker in Frame 1, the wearer's partly obscured left hand and foot in Frame 4, the other standing worker in Frame 5, and every hand skeleton belonging to the distant workers.
